page: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-128GB is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong computational capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations fall within the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is also strong, with read-only large block speeds reaching 235.89 GB/sec and write speeds at 118.27 GB/sec. However, the server exhibits weak performance in LLM inference tasks, with text generation speeds for a small 135M model placing in the bottom 10% tier.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a cost-effective option for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under noisy-neighbor conditions. Given its strong database operation benchmarks and substantial local SSD storage, this server is well-suited for relational databases, multi-threaded data processing, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
